headline: Cool, mainly dry weather settles over Central Kentucky while repeated heavy rain threatens the Upstate through Sunday night
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Post-frontal northeast flow keeps Danville and the Bluegrass cool and mainly dry. A weak disturbance may brush southern Kentucky with a light shower late tonight or early Sunday, but the main story is clearing, comfortable afternoons and increasingly cool nights through Monday.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: No significant hazard expected; a stray light shower is possible south of Danville late tonight
days.forecast: Partly to mostly sunny for the rest of the afternoon with a steady northeast breeze around 7–12 mph. Temperatures top out near 70, with cooler readings south of Lexington. Clouds increase tonight, and a weak disturbance may produce a brief light shower toward Lake Cumberland, but Danville should remain predominantly dry.

days.label: Sunday
days.forecast: A stray early shower cannot be ruled out south or southeast of Danville. Otherwise, clouds gradually thin and most of the day stays dry with a light north to northeast wind. Guidance differs on afternoon warming, so the range is wider than usual; the coolest outcome would occur if low clouds linger longer. Skies clear Sunday night, allowing a sharp temperature drop into the upper 40s.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: A few sheltered rural locations may approach the upper 30s Monday night
days.forecast: Sunny and dry under high pressure. Northeast winds increase to around 7–12 mph during the afternoon. The NWS and NAM retain lower-70s temperatures while GFS and ECMWF guidance is several degrees warmer, so confidence in the exact high is moderate. Clear skies and dry air support a chilly Monday night, with the coolest valleys near 40.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky is entering a quiet, cool stretch. Aside from a very small late-tonight or early-Sunday shower chance south of Danville, the forecast is dry. Highs stay mainly in the 70s, while clear skies allow lows to fall into the upper 40s Sunday night and near 40 in the coolest locations Monday night.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry conditions and cool nights; moderate on Sunday and Monday afternoon temperatures because global guidance is warmer than the NWS and mesoscale guidance

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: Showers and thunderstorms become numerous around Clemson and Central this afternoon and evening, followed by widespread rain in a cool northeast-flow wedge tonight through Sunday night. Repeated heavy showers may cause localized flooding before rain exits early Monday.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: Heavy rain and isolated thunderstorms may cause localized flooding; organized severe weather is unlikely
days.forecast: Showers and thunderstorms become increasingly numerous this afternoon as a back-door front meets humid southwest flow. Slow-moving cells may produce locally heavy rain, especially from late afternoon through evening. Rain becomes more widespread tonight as northeast flow strengthens and a cold-air-damming wedge develops.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: Localized flooding is possible where repeated heavy showers overlap Saturday rainfall
days.forecast: Cloudy, cool and wet. A brief morning lull is possible, but another period of widespread rain and embedded thunderstorms develops during the afternoon and evening. Many locations receive another 1–2 inches in the heavier corridor, although exact placement remains uncertain. The temperature range is deliberately wide because NAM, GFS and RAP guidance maintains a stronger cool wedge than ECMWF.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: Wet roads and isolated residual flooding early; no organized severe-weather threat
days.forecast: A lingering shower is possible near daybreak, then the upper disturbance moves east and the wedge erodes. Clouds gradually break, allowing temperatures to rebound into the middle or upper 70s. Monday night turns mostly clear and noticeably cooler; KLQK and other sheltered cold pockets may fall several degrees below Clemson and KCEU.

upstate.bottomLine: The highest-impact period is this afternoon through Sunday night. Two rounds of heavy rain may overlap, creating localized flooding even though no Flood Watch is in effect at issuance. Sunday stays much cooler beneath a northeast-flow wedge. Rain exits early Monday, followed by clearing and a cooler Monday night.
upstate.confidence: High that rain becomes widespread and heavy at times; moderate on the location of the heaviest totals; moderate-low on Sunday temperatures because the ECMWF is materially warmer than the stronger-wedge guidance

sourceNotes: NWS point forecasts for Danville and Clemson were generated at approximately 1:02 PM EDT. Official airport observations span 12:35–12:45 PM EDT, and the forecast data collection completed at 1:03 PM EDT.

The Louisville and Greenville-Spartanburg Area Forecast Discussions were issued at 6:39 AM and 2:29 AM EDT, respectively. Louisville supports a dry, cool weekend outside a small southern-Kentucky shower chance and much cooler nights early next week. Greenville-Spartanburg supports numerous Saturday thunderstorms, widespread rain through Sunday night, a cold-air-damming wedge and localized flooding potential, while noting that event-total rainfall trended downward.

The NWS active-alert API returned no active alerts for either the Danville or Clemson forecast point at the approximately 1:03 PM EDT check. This official-alert status is separate from the independent heavy-rain and localized-flooding analysis.

Model inventories checked at approximately 1:02 PM EDT showed the complete 15Z HRRR through forecast hour 18, complete 15Z RAP through hour 51, 12Z NAM through hour 84, NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 12Z GFS through hour 333, and the 12Z GEFS mean through hour 174. The latest complete ECMWF deterministic cycle was 06Z through hour 144. Every selected run covers the portion of the forecast for which it is used.

College of DuPage NEXLAB radar and clean-infrared satellite panels were inspected around 1:04 PM EDT. Radar showed active showers and thunderstorms across parts of the Carolinas with lighter echoes farther west, while infrared imagery showed a broad cloud and moisture shield from the Gulf states through the Carolinas. Central Kentucky was behind the primary convective corridor.

College of DuPage model panels show meaningful temperature spread. RAP, NAM and GFS maintain a stronger cool wedge in the Upstate Sunday, while ECMWF is several degrees warmer. GFS and ECMWF are also warmer than the NWS and NAM near Danville Monday. Forecast ranges were widened and confidence lowered to preserve this uncertainty rather than forcing an unsupported single solution.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.

The latest available cumulative accuracy summary was consulted from the forecast-accuracy-feedback branch because forecast-accuracy.json is not yet present on main. Central Kentucky nighttime ranges were shifted modestly lower where the KDVK bias applies; Upstate highs were tempered and nighttime ranges widened downward for KLQK. Day-three ranges were widened because historical 72-hour coverage is weakest, and small residual precipitation probabilities were retained because the 0–20% reliability bin has verified wetter than forecast.
Radar and satellite links remain external and live; the existing website radar section is not modified by this candidate.

appliedAdjustments.details: Shifted overnight ranges about 1–2°F lower where the KDVK low-temperature signal applies and widened later ranges because historical 72-hour coverage is weakest. Daytime ranges remain centered on current guidance because KLEX does not share the smaller KDVK daytime bias.

Tempered daytime ceilings and widened nighttime ranges downward to represent KLQK's recurring cold-pocket behavior. The full station-specific KLQK correction was not imposed across the entire Clemson region, especially during the cloudy and wet wedge.

Retained nonzero residual precipitation probabilities where uncertainty exists because the verified 0–20% bin has observed precipitation more often than forecast, and widened ranges where model spread is materially larger than the historical range width.
